classes.name: Eleição do Presidente da República
classes.finest_note: Parish and consular post on the Ministry's sites from 2001; district in CNE's maps for 1976-1996.
classes.note: Direct two-round election: a candidate needs more than half of the valid votes, otherwise the two leading candidates meet in a second round (Constitution art. 126.º); five-year term (art. 128.º), one consecutive re-election.

cadence.runoff_rule: The two leading candidates meet in a second ballot within 21 days (Constitution art. 126.º)
cadence.administered_by: Ministério da Administração Interna and the Comissão Nacional de Eleições
cadence.locator: Constituição, arts. 126.º and 128.º (O mandato do Presidente da República tem a duração de cinco anos)
cadence.vacancy_rule: A new election within 60 days; the newly elected President starts a new five-year term (art. 128.º n.º 2)

classes.note: Every parish elects an assembly by list PR; the first candidate of the most-voted list becomes president of the parish executive (junta). Parishes of 150 voters or fewer meet as a plenário of all voters instead (Lei n.º 169/99, art. 21.º).

cadence.vacancy_rule: A vacant seat passes to the next candidate on the same list; when a body can no longer be completed, an intercalary election is held within 60 days (art. 222.º)

classes.name: Eleições autárquicas intercalares
classes.finest_note: CNE publishes each intercalary election's official map; the Ministry's sites carry only the 2007 Lisbon chamber by-election.
classes.note: Held within 60 days when a municipal chamber, municipal assembly, or parish assembly can no longer be completed or is dissolved; the body serves out the remaining term (Lei Orgânica n.º 1/2001, arts. 220.º and 222.º). CNE lists 562 such acts from 1978 to 2027, mostly parish assemblies (538), with 23 chambers and one municipal assembly.

classes.name: Eleições para as Cortes e a Câmara dos Deputados (1820-1910)
classes.name_en: Cortes and Chamber of Deputies elections (1820-1910)
classes.note: From the indirect election of the constituent Cortes in December 1820 (parish, comarca, and province juntas, after the Cádiz system) through the census-suffrage Chambers of Deputies of the constitutional monarchy; the Chamber of Peers was appointed or hereditary.

dates.quote: Todo este intrincado processo eleitoral das primeiras eleições portuguesas ficou concluído no dia de Natal de 1820
dates.note: Indirect election of the Cortes Gerais, Extraordinárias e Constituintes.
Elections to the Cortes and the Chamber of Deputies under the 1822 Constitution, the 1826 Charter, and the 1838 Constitution; not yet counted from the Assembly's historical records.

classes.name: Assembleia Nacional Constituinte (1911)
classes.note: Elected in May 1911 by literate men and heads of family over 21, with d'Hondt PR in Lisbon and Porto; it adopted the 1911 Constitution and split into the Chamber of Deputies and the Senate until 1915.

dates.quote: A Assembleia Nacional Constituinte foi eleita num sufrágio em que só houve eleições em cerca de metade dos círculos eleitorais
dates.note: Unopposed circles proclaimed their candidates elected without a vote.

classes.name: Eleições para o Congresso da República (1915-1925)
classes.note: Direct elections of the Chamber of Deputies and the Senate under the 1911 Constitution, from 1915 until the 1926 coup; the 1918 elections followed Sidónio Pais's decree.

dates.note: Congress elections of 1915, 1918, 1919, 1921, 1922, and 1925; not yet counted from the Assembly's historical records.

classes.name: Eleições para a Assembleia Nacional (1934-1973)
classes.note: Estado Novo single-chamber assembly, first elected in 1934 by direct suffrage of citizens over 21 with literacy or tax qualifications; list voting by district, opposition lists withdrew or were barred in most years.

dates.quote: A primeira Assembleia Nacional foi eleita em 1934 por sufrágio direto dos cidadãos maiores de 21 anos ou emancipados

dates.note: Elections of 1938, 1942, 1945, 1949, 1953, 1957, 1961, 1965, 1969, and 1973; not yet counted from the Assembly's records.

classes.name: Plebiscito constitucional de 1933
classes.note: The 1933 Constitution was approved by plebiscite; abstentions and blank ballots counted as votes in favor.

dates.quote: a Constituição de 1933 foi plebiscitada ... Esta foi a única Constituição a ser aprovada por sufrágio referendário

classes.name: Eleições presidenciais diretas (1918-1958)
classes.note: Sidónio Pais's direct election of April 1918, and the Estado Novo's direct elections of 1928, 1935, 1942, 1949 (no contest after the opposition withdrew), 1951, and 1958 for a seven-year term; the 1959 revision moved the election to an electoral college.

dates.note: Direct presidential elections of 1918, 1928, 1935, 1942, 1949, 1951, and 1958; not yet counted from an official list.

classes.name: Eleição indireta do Presidente da República (1911-1925, 1965-1972)
classes.disposition_reason: Under the 1911 Constitution the Congress elected the President (Bernardino Machado was elected in 1915 and 1925), and after the 1959 revision an electoral college of legislators and local delegates did (1965, 1972); voters had no ballot.

classes.name: Câmara Corporativa (1935-1974)
classes.disposition_reason: A consultative chamber of corporative, local, and cultural representatives designated by their bodies, not elected by voters.

classes.name: Senado eleito pela Constituinte (1911)
classes.name_en: Senate chosen by the Constituent Assembly (1911)
classes.disposition_reason: The 71 senators of 1911 were elected by and from the constituent deputies; no popular vote.

classes.name: Governo e Primeiro-Ministro
classes.disposition_reason: The Prime Minister is appointed by the President in light of the election results; there is no direct election.

classes.name: Governo Regional e Representante da República
classes.name_en: Regional Government and Representative of the Republic
classes.disposition_reason: The regional president is appointed by the Representative of the Republic in light of the election results, and the Representative by the President (Constitution art. 231.º).

classes.name: Presidente da câmara municipal
classes.disposition_reason: The mayor is the first candidate of the most-voted list for the municipal chamber (Constitution art. 239.º n.º 3); the camara_municipal class holds that contest.

classes.name: Junta de freguesia
classes.disposition_reason: The junta's president is the head of the most-voted list for the parish assembly and its members are chosen by the assembly (Lei n.º 169/99); the assembleia_freguesia class holds the vote.

classes.name: Plenário de cidadãos eleitores
classes.disposition_reason: In parishes of 150 voters or fewer the assembly is replaced by a plenary meeting of all voters (Lei n.º 169/99, art. 21.º), which elects the junta's president by a show of hands or open vote; there is no ballot or published result.

classes.name: Assembleias distritais
classes.disposition_reason: District assemblies are composed of municipal representatives (Constitution art. 291.º n.º 2), not elected by voters.

classes.name: Áreas metropolitanas e comunidades intermunicipais
classes.disposition_reason: Their councils are formed by the member municipalities' chamber presidents and assemblies (Lei n.º 75/2013); no direct election.

classes.name: Regiões administrativas
classes.disposition_reason: The Constitution provides elected regional assemblies (arts. 255.º-262.º), but the regions were rejected in the 8 November 1998 referendum and have never been instituted.

classes.name: Magistrados e juízes do Tribunal Constitucional
classes.disposition_reason: Judges are career magistrates; ten of the thirteen Constitutional Court judges are chosen by the Assembly of the Republic and three co-opted. Voters elect none.

classes.name: Escolha de candidatos pelos partidos
classes.disposition_reason: Parties choose their lists under their own statutes; the state runs no primary and publishes no nominating vote.

classes.name: Assembleia Legislativa de Macau (1976-1999)
classes.disposition_reason: Macau's elections under Portuguese administration belong to Macau's own census (MO in the world tier); Portugal's own voters in Macau voted in the Fora da Europa circle (Lei n.º 14/79, art. 12.º n.º 4).

classes.name: Conselhos legislativos e eleições ultramarinas
classes.disposition_reason: Elections held in the former overseas provinces (Angola, Mozambique, Cape Verde, Guinea, São Tomé, Goa, Timor) belong to those countries' own censuses.

classes.name: Comissões de trabalhadores, ordens profissionais e outras eleições internas
classes.name_en: Workers' committees, professional orders, and other internal elections
classes.disposition_reason: Held inside workplaces, unions, and professional orders under their own statutes; the state publishes no results.

classes.name: Eleições municipais e paroquiais (1822-1974)
classes.disposition_reason: Municipal councils were elected under the monarchy and the First Republic (the Estado Novo appointed mayors and elected councils by corporative suffrage), but no official register lists these elections or their results; they sit in municipal minutes and the regional press.
